blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Capacitor:  A capacitor or condenser consists of two conductors separated by an insulator or dielectric. can  It is a device which store energy in electric field.

Electrical Capacitance: It is the capacity of the capacitor/conductor to store charge.

$Q \propto V, Q=C V$

$\mathrm{C}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{~V}} \Rightarrow \text { constant }$

Capacitance :

Capacitance of conductor depends upon shape, size, presence of medium.

The capacitance depends only on the geometry of the conductors and not charge given to conductor or potential difference.

SI Unit-Coulomb/volt or Farad (F)

$\text { Dimensional formula of capacitance } \Rightarrow\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-2} \mathrm{~T}^4 \mathrm{~A}^2\right]$

Principle of Capacitor: When uncharged conductor is placed nearer to the charged conductor and uncharged conductor is connected to earth, then capacitance of charged conductor increase.

Capacitance of an isolated Spherical Conductor :

$\text { Capacitance of an isolated spherical conductor } \rightarrow C=4 \pi \epsilon_0 R$

If the medium around the conductor is a dielectric of constant K from surface of sphere to infinity then $\mathrm{C}_{\text {medium }}=4 \pi \in_0 \mathrm{KR}$

Capacitance of spherical capacitor :-

(a) Outer sphere is earthed :

$C=\dfrac{Q}{V_1-V_2}=\dfrac{Q}{\dfrac{K Q}{a}-\dfrac{K Q}{b}}=\dfrac{a b}{K(b-a)}=\dfrac{4 \pi \epsilon_0 a b}{b-a}=\dfrac{4 \pi \epsilon_0 a b}{b-a}$

(b) Inner sphere is earthed :

$\mathrm{C}=\dfrac{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~b}^2}{\mathrm{~b}-\mathrm{a}}$

Cylindrical Capacitor :

$\text { Capacitance per unit length }=\dfrac{2 \pi \epsilon_0}{\ln \dfrac{b}{a}} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}$

$\text { Capacitance, } \mathrm{C}=\dfrac{2 \pi \varepsilon_0 \ell}{\ln (\mathrm{~b} / \mathrm{a})}$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Work Done by External Agent to Charge a Conductor

$\mathrm{W}=\dfrac{\mathrm{q}_2^2-\mathrm{q}_1^2}{2 \mathrm{C}}$ $\text { where } q_1 \rightarrow \text { initial charge, } q_2 \rightarrow \text { final charge }$

work done by an external agent to increase the potential of the conductor from $V_1 \text { to } V_2\\$$\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{C}\left(\mathrm{~V}_2^2-\mathrm{V}_1^2\right)$

Energy stored in a capacitor

The potential energy of a conductor which to charged by potential V given by

$ \mathrm{U}=\dfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2=\dfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{QV}=\dfrac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}}$

The potential energy of the conducting sphere is given by $\mathrm{U}=\dfrac{\mathrm{k} \mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{R}}=\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{R}}$

Potential Energy Stored in Capacitor

$\begin{aligned} &\text { As we know that W.D.ext }=\Delta U\\ &\left[\mathrm{U}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}^2}{2 \mathrm{C}}\right] \quad\left[\mathrm{U}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2\right] \quad\left[\mathrm{U}=\frac{\mathrm{QV}}{2}\right] \end{aligned}$

Parallel plate capacitor: It consists of two large plane parallel conducting plates separated by a small distance.

Capacitance of Parallel Plate Capacitor :

$C_0=\frac{Q}{V} =\frac{\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}$

Capacitance of Parallel Plate Capacitor (PPC) depends on

$\text { (i) Overlapping area } \Rightarrow \mathrm{C} \propto \mathrm{~A}$

$\text { (ii) Distance between plates } \Rightarrow \mathrm{C} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~d}}$

$\text { (iii) Medium between plates } \Rightarrow \mathrm{C} \propto \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}$

Note:  Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor does not depend on thickness and nature of metal of plates.

Capacitance of Parallel Plate Capacitor with dielectric:

Capacitance of a capacitor in presence of medium

$C_m=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r A}{d}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}} C_0$

$C_0 \rightarrow \text{ Capacitance of air filled Capacitor}$

Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor when dielectric is partially filled :

Capacitance,

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{(\mathrm{~d}-\mathrm{t})+\dfrac{\mathrm{t}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}}$

In case of multiple slabs,

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\left( d - (t_1 + t_2 + \dots) + \frac{t_1}{\varepsilon_r'} + \dfrac{t_2}{\varepsilon_r''} + \dots \right)}
$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Sharing Of Charges:
When two charged conductors of capacitance $C_1 $ & $C_2$  at potential $V_1 $ & $V_2$ respectively, are connected by a conducting wire, the charge flows from a higher potential conductor to a lower potential conductor until the potential of the two condensers becomes equal. The common potential (V) after sharing of charges;

(1) When the positive plate of one is connected to a positive plate of another, then common potential.

$V=\frac{\text { net charge }}{\text { net capacitance }}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_1+\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1+\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2}$

Charges after sharing $q_1 = C_1V $ & $q_2 = C_2V$. In this process, energy is lost in the connecting wire as heat. This loss of energy is:

$\mathrm{U}_{\text {initital }}-\mathrm{U}_{\text {final }}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{C}_2}{2\left(\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2\right)}\left(\mathrm{V}_1-\mathrm{V}_2\right)^2$

(2) When positive plate of one is connected with negative plate of another, the common potential.

$V_C=\dfrac{C_1 V_1-C_2 V_2}{C_1+C_2}$

$\dfrac{\mathrm{q}_1}{\mathrm{q}_2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{C}_1}{\mathrm{C}_2}$

This loss of energy is:

$\mathrm{U}_{\text {initial }}-\mathrm{U}_{\text {final }}=\dfrac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{C}_2}{2\left(\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2\right)}\left(\mathrm{V}_1+\mathrm{V}_2\right)^2$

Charging of PPC by battery: When a capacitor is charged by a battery then battery charges it till its potential difference becomes equal to EMF of battery.

From conservation of energy

$\mathrm{W}_{\text {by battery }}=\Delta U+\text { Heat loss }$

$\mathrm{CV}^2=\left(\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2-0\right)+\text { heat loss } \Rightarrow \text { Heat loss }=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2$

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question: Initially a uncharged capacitor having capacitance C is connected across a battery of emf V. Now the capacitor is disconnected and then reconnected across the same battery but with reversed polarity. Find heat loss in this process.
blocks.answer:
$\text { Total charge flow } Q_f-Q_i=(C V-(-C V))=2 C V$

$\text { W.D. by battery }=(2 \mathrm{CV})(\mathrm{V})=2 \mathrm{CV}^2$

$\text { Heat loss = W.D. by battery - (Change in Energy stored) }$

$=2 \mathrm{CV}^2-\left(\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2\right)=2 \mathrm{CV}^2$

Salient features of series combination :

(a) All capacitors will have same charge but can have different potential difference across them.

(b) Potential difference across capacitor is inversely proportional to its capacitance in series combination.

(C) In series combination the smallest capacitor gets maximum potential difference.

(d) In series combination equivalent capacitance is always less than the smallest capacitor of combination.

Parallel Combination:

$C_{e q}=C_1+C_2+C_3$

Salient Features of Parallel Combination :

(a) All capacitors have same potential difference but can have different charges.

(b) The charge on the capacitor is proportional to its capacitance.

(c) Maximum charge will flow through the capacitor of largest value.

(d) Equivalent capacitance is always greater than the largest capacitor of combination.

modules.name: Q,V,E,C,U Section and Polar And Non-Polar Dielectrics

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
• Polar Dielectrics
  • In absence of an external field the centres of positive and negative charge do not coincide-due to asymmetric shape of molecules.Each molecule has permanent dipole moment. The dipole are randomly oriented so average dipole moment per unit volume of polar dielectric in absence of external field is nearly zero.In presence of external field dipoles tends to align in direction of field.
  • Example- Water, Alcohol CO2, NH3
Dipole moment of polar molecules depends on temperature :

  • Non Polar Dielectric
  • In the absence of an external field the centre of positive and negative charge coincides in these atoms or molecules because they are symmetric.The dipole moment is zero in normal state.In the presence of an external field they acquire induced dipole moments.
  • Example: Nitrogen, Oxygen, Benzene, Methane
  • Induced electric dipole moment of non-polar molecules is independent of temperature.
Dielectrics: The insulators in which microscopic local displacement of charges takes place in presence of electric field are known as dielectrics. Dielectrics are non-conductors upto certain value of field depending on its nature. If the field exceeds this limiting value called dielectric strength they lose their insulating property and begin to conduct.

Dielectric Strength- It defined as the maximum value of electric field that a dielectric can tolerate without breakdown.

Polarisation :

Polarisation is defined as the electric dipole moment per unit volume.

For linear isotropic dielectrics,

Polarisation (P) of dielectrics is directly proportional to the electric field (E), i.e.,

$ \begin{gathered} P \propto E \\ P=\varepsilon_0 \chi_e E \end{gathered} $

Where, $\chi_{\mathrm{e}} \Rightarrow$ electric susceptibility (constant)

For vacuum, $\chi_{\mathrm{e}}=0$

$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}=\mathrm{n} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\mathrm{qib}}{\mathrm{Ad}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{qi}}{\mathrm{~A}}\right)=\sigma_{\mathrm{i}}=\text { induced surface charge density. }$

blocks.title: Example-1
blocks.question:
Q. A 10 μF capacitor is charged to a potential of 12 V by a battery. After charging, the battery is disconnected.
(a) What is the charge on the capacitor?
(b) What is the energy stored in the capacitor?
(c) If the plates are now pulled apart so that the capacitance becomes 5 μF, what is the new potential across the plates?$$
blocks.answer:
Answer:(a)$1.2 \times 10^{-4} C$

(b)$0.72 \mathrm{~mJ} $

(c) $24 \mathrm{~V}$

Explanation:

Given:

$ C_1=10 \mu F=10 \times 10^{-6} F, V=12 V$

$\text { Battery disconnected } \Rightarrow \text { charge remains constant }$

$\text { (a) } Q=C \cdot V=10 \times 10^{-6} \cdot 12=1.2 \times 10^{-4} C$

$\displaystyle \begin{aligned} &\text { (b) }\\ &U=\frac{1}{2} C V^2=\frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \times 10^{-6} \cdot(12)^2=0.72 \times 10^{-3} J=0.72 \mathrm{~mJ} \end{aligned}$

$\text { (c) New capacitance } C_2=5 \mu F \text {, charge remains } Q=1.2 \times 10^{-4} C$

New voltage

$\displaystyle V^{\prime}=\frac{Q}{C_2}=\frac{1.2 \times 10^{-4}}{5 \times 10^{-6}}=24 \mathrm{~V}$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Effects of Dielectrics in Capacitor :-

Distance Division :

  • Distance is Divided and area remains same
  • Capacitors are in Series
  • Individual Capacitance are
$\mathrm{C}_1=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}_1} \quad \mathrm{C}_2=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}_2}$

  • Effective Capacitance is given by
$\mathrm{C}=\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}\left[\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}}{\mathrm{~d}_1 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}+\mathrm{d}_2 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1}}\right]$

$\text { Special case: If } \mathrm{d}_1=\mathrm{d}_2=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}\left|\frac{2 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}}\right|$

Area Division :

  • Area is divided and distance remains same
  • Capacitors are in Parallel
  • Individual capacitors are
$\mathrm{C}_1=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \mathrm{~A}_1}{\mathrm{~d}} \quad \mathrm{C}_2=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2} \mathrm{~A}_2}{\mathrm{~d}}$

  • Effective Capacitance is given by
$C=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} A_1}{d}+\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2} A_2}{d}$

$\text { Special Case: If } A_1=A_2=\frac{A}{2} \Rightarrow C=\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}\left(\frac{\epsilon_{r 1}+\epsilon_{r 2}}{2}\right)$

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Formulae for charging of capacitor

Charge on Capacitor at any time t

$\begin{aligned} &\mathrm{q}=\mathrm{EC}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{\tau}}\right) \\ & \text { here } \tau=\mathrm{RC} \text { is known as time constant. } \end{aligned}$

After one time constant i.e. at $\mathrm{t}=\tau$

• Current at any time

$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{dq}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{R}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}} \end{aligned}$

• Potential difference across capacitor plates at any time t

$V_C=\frac{q}{C}=E\left(1-e^{-t / R C}\right)$

• Potential difference across resistor at any time t

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{iR}=\mathrm{Ee}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}} $

Heat dissipated:

From Energy Conservation

$\text { Heat dissipated = work done by battery }-\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\text {capacitor }}$

Derivation of equation of discharging circuit:

Change at any time :

$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{q}=\mathrm{q}_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}}$

$\text { Current at any time, }= \mathrm{i}=-\frac{\mathrm{dq}}{\mathrm{dt}}= \mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_0}{\mathrm{RC}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}}$

Potential difference across the condenser at any time, $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_0}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{e}^{-t / \operatorname{RC}}$

Potential difference across the resistor at any time, $ V_R=i R=\frac{q_0}{C} e^{-t / R C}$

$V=\frac{\text { net charge }}{\text { net capacitance }}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_1+\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1+\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2}$

Charges after sharing $q_1 = C_1V $ & $q_2 = C_2V$. In this process, energy is lost in the connecting wire as heat. This loss of energy is:

$\mathrm{U}_{\text {initital }}-\mathrm{U}_{\text {final }}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{C}_2}{2\left(\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2\right)}\left(\mathrm{V}_1-\mathrm{V}_2\right)^2$

(2) When positive plate of one is connected with negative plate of another, the common potential.

$V_C=\dfrac{C_1 V_1-C_2 V_2}{C_1+C_2}$

$\dfrac{\mathrm{q}_1}{\mathrm{q}_2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{C}_1}{\mathrm{C}_2}$

This loss of energy is:

$\mathrm{U}_{\text {initial }}-\mathrm{U}_{\text {final }}=\dfrac{\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{C}_2}{2\left(\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2\right)}\left(\mathrm{V}_1+\mathrm{V}_2\right)^2$

Charging of PPC by battery: When a capacitor is charged by a battery then battery charges it till its potential difference becomes equal to EMF of battery.

From conservation of energy

$\mathrm{W}_{\text {by battery }}=\Delta U+\text { Heat loss }$

$\mathrm{CV}^2=\left(\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2-0\right)+\text { heat loss } \Rightarrow \text { Heat loss }=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{CV}^2$

blocks.text:
Effects of Dielectrics in Capacitor :-

Distance Division :

  • Distance is Divided and area remains same
  • Capacitors are in Series
  • Individual Capacitance are
$\mathrm{C}_1=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}_1} \quad \mathrm{C}_2=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}_2}$

  • Effective Capacitance is given by
$\mathrm{C}=\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}\left[\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}}{\mathrm{~d}_1 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}+\mathrm{d}_2 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1}}\right]$

$\text { Special case: If } \mathrm{d}_1=\mathrm{d}_2=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}\left|\frac{2 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2}}\right|$

Area Division :

  • Area is divided and distance remains same
  • Capacitors are in Parallel
  • Individual capacitors are
$\mathrm{C}_1=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} \mathrm{~A}_1}{\mathrm{~d}} \quad \mathrm{C}_2=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2} \mathrm{~A}_2}{\mathrm{~d}}$

  • Effective Capacitance is given by
$C=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_1} A_1}{d}+\frac{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}_2} A_2}{d}$

$\text { Special Case: If } A_1=A_2=\frac{A}{2} \Rightarrow C=\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}\left(\frac{\epsilon_{r 1}+\epsilon_{r 2}}{2}\right)$

Formulae for charging of capacitor

Charge on Capacitor at any time t

$\begin{aligned} &\mathrm{q}=\mathrm{EC}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{\tau}}\right) \\ & \text { here } \tau=\mathrm{RC} \text { is known as time constant. } \end{aligned}$

After one time constant i.e. at $\mathrm{t}=\tau$

• Current at any time

$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{dq}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{R}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}} \end{aligned}$

• Potential difference across capacitor plates at any time t

$V_C=\frac{q}{C}=E\left(1-e^{-t / R C}\right)$

• Potential difference across resistor at any time t

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{iR}=\mathrm{Ee}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}} $

Heat dissipated:

From Energy Conservation

$\text { Heat dissipated = work done by battery }-\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\text {capacitor }}$

Derivation of equation of discharging circuit:

Change at any time :

$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{q}=\mathrm{q}_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}}$

$\text { Current at any time, }= \mathrm{i}=-\frac{\mathrm{dq}}{\mathrm{dt}}= \mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_0}{\mathrm{RC}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{t} / \mathrm{RC}}$

Potential difference across the condenser at any time, $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_0}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{e}^{-t / \operatorname{RC}}$

Potential difference across the resistor at any time, $ V_R=i R=\frac{q_0}{C} e^{-t / R C}$
